text: sternocleidomastoid
the long muscle at the side of your neck
Let your head be heavy; you don’t need to hold it up with your neck.
Soften the sides of your neck and let the jaw unclench.
In the twist, turn your gaze last, and keep the neck long.
trapezius
the top of your shoulders and upper back
Relax your shoulders away from your ears.
Slide your shoulder blades down your back.
Let the tops of your shoulders melt away from your neck.
In Downward Dog, broaden across the upper back rather than shrugging.
levator scapulae
the muscle that lifts your shoulder blade
Drop your ear toward your shoulder and let the back of the neck lengthen.
Keep your shoulder blades heavy as you reach up.
rhomboids
the muscles between your shoulder blades
Draw your shoulder blades toward each other and lift your chest.
In Locust, squeeze between the shoulder blades to lift the arms higher.
Round your upper back and let the space between your shoulder blades open.
deltoids
the caps of your shoulders
Reach out through your fingertips; let the shoulders stay soft while the arms work.
In Warrior II, keep the arms at shoulder height, strong to the fingertips.
Let the arms rest; nothing to hold here.
rotator cuff
the small muscles that hold your shoulder in its socket
Rotate your upper arms outward so the shoulders feel wide.
In Chaturanga, keep the elbows close and the shoulders no lower than the elbows.
If the shoulder pinches, come out and choose the gentler option.
teres major
the muscle under your armpit at the back
Lift your armpits toward the ceiling in Downward Dog.
pectoralis major
your chest
Open your chest toward the ceiling.
Broaden across your collarbones.
Lower to Chaturanga with your chest, not your chin.
Let the front of your chest soften and spread over the bolster.
pectoralis minor
the small muscle under your chest
Let your arms open wide and feel the space under your collarbones.
Lift the front of your shoulders away from the floor.
serratus anterior
the muscle along the side of your ribs
Push the floor away and feel your upper back broaden.
In Plank, don’t let your chest sink between your shoulders.
Wrap your shoulder blades around your ribs.
latissimus dorsi
the big muscles of your mid back
Reach your arms up and feel the sides of your back lengthen.
In Downward Dog, send your hips back and let the sides of your waist get long.
In the side bend, breathe into the side ribs.
erector spinae
the long muscles along your spine
Lengthen your spine from your tailbone to the crown of your head.
Lift through the back of your heart in Locust.
Let your back round; let the muscles along your spine go quiet.
Keep a long spine as you fold; hinge from your hips.
quadratus lumborum
the deep muscle of your lower back and waist
Let the waist on your top side open and breathe into it.
Keep both hips level as you reach over to the side.
biceps
the front of your upper arms
Keep a soft bend in your elbows; don’t lock them.
In Chaturanga, bend your elbows to ninety degrees, no lower.
triceps
the back of your upper arms
Press the floor away and straighten your arms without locking your elbows.
Hug your elbows in toward your ribs as you lower.
Let the arms be heavy; you don’t need them here.
forearm flexors
the inside of your forearms
Spread your fingers wide and press through your knuckles.
Turn your palms up and stretch the inside of your wrists.
forearm extensors
the outside of your forearms
Grip the mat lightly with your fingertips to protect your wrists.
rectus abdominis
the front of your belly
Draw your lower ribs in toward your hips.
In Boat, lift your chest and keep the belly firm, not hard.
In Sphinx, let the belly be soft and the front body long.
Knit your front ribs together as you reach up.
obliques
the sides of your waist
Twist from your belly, not from your neck.
Lengthen first, then twist a little more on each exhale.
In Side Plank, lift your waist away from the floor.
Let the twist happen without pulling; the breath does the work.
internal oblique
the deeper layer of your waist
Draw your navel gently toward your spine as you twist.
transversus abdominis
your deep belly, like a corset
Draw your belly in gently to support your spine.
Engage uddiyana bandha: lift and draw in just below the navel.
Hug your low belly in as you lift one leg.
diaphragm
your breathing muscle, under your ribs
Breathe low into your belly; let your ribs widen on the inhale.
Keep the breath steady and audible; let it lead the movement.
Inhale, feel your ribs expand in every direction.
pelvic floor
the floor of your pelvis
Engage mula bandha: a gentle lift at the base of the pelvis.
Let the pelvic floor soften and widen as you breathe out.
iliopsoas
your deep hip flexors
Sink your hips forward and down, and feel the front of your back hip open.
In Dragon, let the weight of the hips do the work; breathe into the front of the hip.
Tuck your tailbone slightly to lengthen the front of your hips.
In Boat, lift from deep in your hips, not just your belly.
tensor fasciae latae
the muscle at the outer front of your hip
Soften the outer hip of your standing leg; don’t grip.
In Shoelace, let the outer hips release toward the floor.
gluteus maximus
your seat
Press into your heels and lift your hips.
In Bridge, keep the glutes working but not clenched.
Let your seat get heavy and soft; sink toward the floor.
Squeeze your seat gently to protect your lower back in the backbend.
gluteus medius
the side of your hip
Keep your hips level; don’t let the standing hip push out.
Press the outer edge of your back foot down and feel the side of your hip wake up.
In Shoelace, breathe into the outer hip.
gluteus minimus
the small deep muscle of your outer hip
Steady your standing hip without gripping.
piriformis
deep in your outer hip
You should feel this deep in your outer hip, not in your knee.
Find your edge and let the hip soften a little more with each exhale.
Flex your front foot to protect the knee as the hip opens.
deep hip rotators
the small muscles deep in your hip
Let the thighs roll open from deep in the hip sockets.
Rotate your front thigh out as you fold.
adductors
your inner thighs
Squeeze the block between your thighs.
In Frog, let your inner thighs soften toward the floor; don’t push.
In Prasarita, draw your inner thighs back as you fold.
Let your inner thighs open as you sink into Warrior II.
sartorius
the long strap muscle across your thigh
Open your knee out to the side as you place the foot in Tree.
quadriceps
the front of your thighs
Lift your kneecaps to engage the front of your thighs.
In Chair, sit back into your heels and feel your thighs working.
In Saddle, let the front of your thighs lengthen; come up if the knees complain.
Press through your front foot and feel the front of your thigh working.
hamstrings
the back of your thighs
Bend your knees as much as you need to keep your back long.
Lift your sitting bones toward the ceiling in Downward Dog.
In Caterpillar, let your back round and the backs of your legs soften.
Fold from your hips, not from your waist.
IT band
the thick band down the outside of your thigh
Cross your knees and let the outer thighs release.
In Eagle, hug your thighs together and feel the outer hips.
tibialis anterior
the front of your shin
Flex your feet and pull your toes toward you.
In Toe Squat and Hero, let the fronts of the shins and ankles stretch slowly.
calves
the back of your lower legs
Reach your heels toward the floor; they don’t have to touch.
Pedal your feet to wake up your calves.
In Squat, let your heels sink; use a blanket under them if they lift.
tibialis posterior
the deep muscle that holds up your arch
Lift your inner arches and press the base of your big toes down.
fibularis longus
the outside of your lower leg
Spread your toes and feel the four corners of your foot.
Achilles tendon
the cord above your heel
Let your heels sink slowly; never bounce.
plantar fascia
the sole of your foot
Tuck your toes under and sit back on your heels. Stay with the breath.
Spread your toes and press evenly through the sole of your foot.
crown of the head
the top of your head
Lengthen through the crown of your head.
Reach the crown of your head forward as you fold.
Let the crown of your head be heavy toward the floor.
jaw
your jaw
Unclench your jaw; let your teeth part slightly.
Soften your jaw and the space between your eyebrows.
cervical spine
your neck
Keep the back of your neck long; gaze slightly forward, not up.
In Shoulderstand, never turn your head.
Let your neck be in line with your spine; a folded blanket under the head helps.
thoracic spine
your upper back
Lift your chest and open across your upper back.
Let the upper back round over the bolster.
Twist from your upper back, not your lower back.
lumbar spine
your lower back
Keep your lower back long; don’t let it collapse.
In backbends, lengthen through the lower back before you bend.
If your lower back complains, bend your knees or come out.
sacrum
the flat bone at the base of your spine
Let your sacrum feel heavy toward the floor.
In Bridge, slide a block under your sacrum, not your lower back.
tailbone
your tailbone
Lengthen your tailbone toward your heels.
Tuck your tailbone slightly in Warrior I.
Let your tailbone drop and the lower back widen.
pelvis
your hips
Keep your hips level, like a bowl of water you don’t want to spill.
Square your hips to the front of the mat.
Let the pelvis settle; there’s nothing to hold.
hip points
the bony points at the front of your hips
Point your hip points forward, like headlights.
Draw your front hip point back and your back hip point forward.
sitting bones
the bones you sit on
Root down through your sitting bones and lengthen up.
Lift your sitting bones toward the ceiling in Downward Dog.
Sit on the edge of a blanket so your sitting bones can tip forward.
pubic bone
the bone at the front of your pelvis
Draw your pubic bone toward your navel to lengthen the lower back.
In Cobra, press your pubic bone into the mat.
hip joint
your hip socket
Hinge at your hips, not your waist.
Let the thigh bone settle deeper into the hip socket.
Turn your thigh out from the hip socket, not the knee.
thigh bone
your thigh bone
Draw your front thigh bone back into the hip socket.
Let the weight of the thigh bones sink.
knee
your knee
Keep your knee tracking over your second toe.
Stack your knee over your ankle, not past it.
If you feel anything sharp in the knee, come out of the pose.
Keep a micro-bend; don’t lock your knees.
kneecap
your kneecap
Lift your kneecaps to engage your thighs.
Soften behind the kneecaps; nothing to hold here.
shin
your shin
Let your shin angle back; it doesn’t need to be parallel to the mat.
Keep your front shin vertical in the lunge.
ankle
your ankle
Stack your knee over your ankle.
Flex your ankle and point your toes toward your face.
In Toe Squat, go gently; the ankles and toes open slowly.
heel
your heel
Root down through your back heel.
Reach your heels toward the floor.
Sit back toward your heels and let the hips rest.
arch of the foot
the arch of your foot
Lift your inner arches and press the base of your big toes down.
Press the four corners of your feet into the mat.
toes
your toes
Spread your toes wide.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips.
Turn your right toes out and your left toes in slightly.
ribs
your ribs
Knit your front ribs in; don’t let them flare.
Breathe into your side ribs and the back of your ribs.
Lift your ribs away from your hips to make space for the twist.
breastbone
the centre of your chest
Lift your sternum toward the ceiling.
In Cobra, lead with your breastbone, not your chin.
Let your sternum soften and sink in the forward fold.
collarbones
your collarbones
Broaden across your collarbones.
Spread your collarbones and draw your shoulder blades down.
shoulder blades
your shoulder blades
Slide your shoulder blades down your back.
Draw your shoulder blades toward each other and lift your chest.
In Plank, spread your shoulder blades wide across your back.
Let your shoulder blades melt down toward the floor.
shoulder
your shoulder
Relax your shoulders away from your ears.
Stack your shoulders over your wrists.
If the shoulder pinches, bring the arm lower.
upper arm bone
your upper arm
Rotate your upper arms outward to make space for your neck.
Hug your upper arms in toward your ribs.
elbow
your elbow
Keep a soft bend in your elbows.
In Chaturanga, bend your elbows straight back, hugging your ribs.
Point your elbow creases forward.
forearm
your forearm
Come down onto your forearms, elbows under your shoulders.
Rest on your forearms or lower all the way down.
wrist
your wrist
Spread your fingers and press through your knuckles to take weight off your wrists.
If your wrists hurt, come onto your fists or your forearms.
Stack your shoulders over your wrists.
hands and fingers
your hands
Spread your fingers wide, middle fingers pointing forward.
Press into the base of your index fingers.
Turn your palms up and let the fingers curl softly.
flexion
bend, fold, curl
Fold forward from your hips.
Bend your knees deeply.
Round your spine and let your head hang.
extension
straighten, lengthen, arch, open
Straighten your front leg and lift your chest.
Press into your hands and arch your upper back.
Let the front of your body open over the bolster.
lateral flexion
side bend
Reach up and over to the right, keeping both hips grounded.
Let your side body lengthen; breathe into the ribs on top.
rotation
twist, turn
Twist from your belly and let your gaze follow last.
Rotate your upper arms outward.
Let the twist deepen on its own with each exhale.
external rotation
turn out, open
Turn your front thigh out so the knee tracks over the toes.
Roll your upper arms out and your shoulder blades down.
Let your knees fall open.
internal rotation
turn in
Roll your back thigh in so the hips face forward.
Turn your palms to face behind you.
abduction
lift out to the side, widen
Reach your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Step your feet wide apart.
Let your legs open wide and heavy in Dragonfly.
adduction
draw in, squeeze together
Squeeze your inner thighs together.
Hug your legs together in Headstand.
plantar flexion
point your foot
Point your toes and reach through the top of your foot.
Let the tops of your feet rest on the floor.
dorsiflexion
flex your foot
Flex your front foot to protect the knee.
Flex your feet and press through your heels.
pronation and supination
turn your palm down / turn your palm up
Turn your palms up and open your chest.
Rest your hands palms up, fingers soft.
protraction and retraction
spread your shoulder blades / squeeze your shoulder blades
Push the floor away and spread your shoulder blades.
Draw your shoulder blades together and lift your heart.
elevation and depression
shrug up / draw down
Draw your shoulders down away from your ears.
Inhale, shrug your shoulders up; exhale, let them drop.
anterior and posterior pelvic tilt
tip your pelvis forward / tuck your tailbone
Tip your pelvis forward and lift your sitting bones.
Tuck your tailbone and round your lower back.
Find a neutral pelvis: hip points and pubic bone in one line.
Mountain Pose
Samasthitiḥ
Come to the front of your mat and stand with your feet together.
Spread your toes and press evenly through both feet.
Lift your kneecaps to wake up the front of your thighs.
Lengthen your tailbone toward your heels and draw your belly in gently.
Let your arms rest by your sides, and lengthen through the crown of your head.
Relax your shoulders away from your ears, and soften your jaw.
Close your mouth and breathe slowly, with a soft sound in your throat.
If your knees tend to push back, keep them very slightly bent.
From here, inhale and reach your arms up.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart if that feels steadier.
Stand with your back to a wall, heels a little away from it, to feel your body line up.
Squeeze a block between your thighs to feel your legs working.
If you feel dizzy, step your feet apart and keep your eyes open.
In pregnancy, stand with your feet hip-width apart or wider.
Upward Salute
Ūrdhva Hastāsana
Inhale, sweep your arms out and up over your head.
Bring your palms together and look up at your thumbs.
Keep your legs strong and your feet rooted.
Draw your lower ribs in so your back doesn’t arch.
Let your shoulders slide down as your arms go up.
Make the movement last the whole inhale.
If your shoulders are tight, keep your hands apart, shoulder-width.
Exhale, fold forward.
Keep your arms shoulder-width apart, palms facing each other.
If your neck is sore, look straight ahead instead of up.
With a shoulder injury, raise your arms only as high as is pain-free.
Don’t throw your head back. Lift your gaze, not your chin.
Standing Forward Fold
Uttānāsana
Exhale, hinge at your hips and fold forward.
Bring your fingertips or palms to the floor beside your feet.
Bend your knees as much as you need to keep your back long.
Lift your sitting bones, and let your head hang heavy.
Shift your weight a little forward, toward the balls of your feet.
Soften the back of your neck, and let your shoulders drop.
Let the exhale fold you a little deeper.
If your lower back complains, bend your knees more.
Inhale, lift your chest halfway and look forward.
Rest your hands on blocks if the floor feels far away.
Hold opposite elbows and let your upper body hang.
Keep your knees well bent and rest your belly on your thighs.
With a lower back injury, bend your knees and come up slowly with a flat back.
If your head feels heavy or dizzy, come up slowly, leading with your chest.
In pregnancy, step your feet wide so your belly has room.
Half Lift
Ardha Uttānāsana
Inhale, come halfway up with your fingertips on the floor.
Lengthen your spine from your tailbone to the crown of your head.
Reach your chest forward and draw your shoulder blades down your back.
Bend your knees if your back starts to round.
Look forward and slightly up, keeping the back of your neck long.
Soften your shoulders. The lift comes from your spine.
It’s one inhale. Don’t hold it here.
With a sore lower back, keep your knees bent and your belly drawn in.
Exhale, plant your hands and step or jump back.
Bring your hands to your shins or to blocks to keep your back flat.
Bend your knees deeply so your spine can stay long.
Keep the back of your neck long. Don’t crank your head up.
If your lower back aches, bend your knees and lift less.
Chaturanga
Caturaṅga Daṇḍāsana
Exhale, step or jump back, and lower halfway down.
Hug your elbows in toward your ribs as you lower.
Keep your elbows stacked over your wrists.
Keep your body in one long line, from your head to your heels.
Stop when your shoulders are level with your elbows.
Let your face stay soft, even while your arms work hard.
One long exhale, all the way down.
Don’t let your shoulders drop lower than your elbows.
Inhale, roll over your toes into Upward Dog.
Lower your knees to the mat first, then bend your elbows.
Place a block under your chest and lower only until you touch it.
Lower all the way to your belly, and skip the hover.
With a shoulder injury, keep your knees down, or skip it and lower to the floor.
If your wrists hurt, press through your knuckles and fingertips.
From the middle of pregnancy, keep your knees down or skip it.
Upward-Facing Dog
Ūrdhva Mukha Śvānāsana
Inhale, roll over your toes and lift your chest forward and up.
Straighten your arms and press the tops of your feet into the mat.
Lift your thighs and knees away from the floor.
Stack your shoulders over your wrists.
Draw your shoulders back and broaden across your collarbones.
Keep your glutes soft, and lengthen your tailbone toward your heels.
Just one inhale here. Let it lift your chest.
If your lower back pinches, bend your elbows a little or lower into Cobra.
Exhale, roll back over your toes into Downward Dog.
Keep your thighs on the mat and lift into Cobra.
Place your hands on blocks to give your lower back more room.
Turn one foot over at a time if rolling over your toes is hard.
Keep the back of your neck long. Don’t drop your head back.
With a lower back injury, take Cobra instead, with your elbows bent.
In pregnancy, skip it: go from all fours straight back into Downward Dog.
Downward-Facing Dog
Adho Mukha Śvānāsana
Exhale, roll over your toes and lift your hips up and back.
Spread your fingers wide and press down through your knuckles.
Let your head hang between your arms, and gaze toward your navel.
Rotate your upper arms outward to make space for your neck.
Reach your heels toward the floor. They don’t have to touch.
Bend your knees as much as you need to keep your back long.
Stay for five breaths. Breathe into the back of your body.
If your shoulders pinch, move your hands a little wider apart.
At the end of your exhale, bend your knees and look between your hands.
Keep your knees bent and your heels lifted if the back of your legs feels tight.
Place your hands on blocks to take weight off your wrists.
Come to your forearms, or rest in Puppy Pose with your knees down.
If your wrists hurt, press through your knuckles and fingertips, not the heel of your hand.
Late in pregnancy, keep the hold short, or choose a gentler option.
Chair Pose
Utkaṭāsana
Inhale, bend your knees and reach your arms up.
Keep your feet and knees together.
Sit back as if into a chair, with your weight in your heels.
Bring your palms together and look up at your thumbs.
Draw your lower ribs in, and lengthen your tailbone down.
Relax your shoulders away from your ears.
Stay for five breaths. Keep the breath long, even when your thighs burn.
If your knees complain, don’t sit as low.
Exhale, fold forward and place your hands beside your feet.
Keep your hands on your hips, or together at your chest.
Squeeze a block between your thighs to keep your knees together.
Rest your back against a wall and slide down only a little.
With a knee injury, bend only a little and keep your weight in your heels.
With a shoulder injury, keep your arms shoulder-width apart, or lower them.
In pregnancy, stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Warrior I
Vīrabhadrāsana I
Turn your back heel down and step your right foot forward between your hands.
Bend your front knee over your ankle.
Press the outer edge of your back foot into the mat.
Turn your hips to face the front of your mat.
Reach your arms up, palms together, and look up at your thumbs.
Let your shoulders drop as your arms reach up.
Stay for five breaths. Sink a little deeper on each exhale.
Keep your front knee over your ankle, not past your toes.
Inhale, straighten your front leg and turn to the other side.
Lift your back heel into a high lunge if your back ankle is tight.
Step your feet wider apart, like train tracks, for more balance.
Keep your hands on your hips if your shoulders are tired.
With a knee injury, bend your front knee less.
If your lower back pinches, draw your belly in and lift your chest less.
With a neck injury, look straight ahead.
Big Toe Pose
Pādāṅguṣṭhāsana
Step or jump your feet hip-width apart, parallel.
Fold and hook your big toes with your first two fingers.
Inhale, straighten your arms and lengthen your spine.
Exhale, bend your elbows out to the sides and fold.
Lift your kneecaps, and lift your sitting bones.
Relax your neck and let your head hang.
Stay for five breaths, gazing toward your nose.
If you feel it right behind your knees, bend them a little.
Inhale, lift your head and straighten your arms.
Bend your knees enough to reach your toes with a long back.
Loop a strap under the balls of your feet and hold that instead.
Rest your hands on your shins.
With a lower back injury, keep your knees bent and your back long. Don’t round to go deeper.
In pregnancy, step your feet wider and keep the fold shallow.
Hand Under Foot Pose
Pādahastāsana
Lift the front of your feet and slide your hands underneath, palms up.
Bring your toes all the way to your wrist creases.
Inhale, straighten your arms and look up.
Exhale, bend your elbows out to the sides and fold deeper.
Shift your weight forward so your hips stay over your feet.
Let your wrists open slowly. Press down only as much as feels good.
Five breaths here. Let each exhale draw your belly in.
If your wrists hurt, slide your hands out a little, or hold your ankles.
Inhale, look up. Exhale, hands to your hips. Inhale, come all the way up.
Bend your knees deeply so your hands slide under easily.
Hold the backs of your ankles instead.
With a wrist injury, skip the hands under your feet and hold your ankles.
With a lower back injury, keep your knees bent and come up with a flat back.
Triangle Pose
Utthita Trikoṇāsana
Step your feet about a leg’s length apart and turn your right toes out.
Line up your front heel with the arch of your back foot.
Reach forward over your right leg, then tip down and hold your big toe.
Stretch your left arm up, in line with your right.
Lengthen both sides of your waist, and open your chest to the side.
Soften your neck, and let your gaze rest on your top hand.
Stay for five breaths, long and smooth.
Don’t lock your front knee. Keep it soft and lifted.
Inhale, come up, and turn to the left.
Rest your bottom hand on a block or on your shin instead of your toe.
Practise with your back against a wall to feel your body in one plane.
If your neck is tired, look straight ahead or down at your front foot.
If your knees tend to push back, keep a soft bend in your front knee.
With a neck injury, look forward, not up.
In pregnancy, shorten your stance and use a block.
Revolved Triangle
Parivṛtta Trikoṇāsana
Turn your right toes out and your back foot in, and square your hips forward.
Exhale, fold over your front leg and bring your left hand outside your right foot.
Press your back heel down and keep your back leg strong.
Draw your right hip back as you twist.
Reach your right arm up and look at your top hand.
Twist from your belly, not from your neck.
Inhale to lengthen, exhale to twist a little more.
Keep your neck long. If it strains, look down at the floor.
Inhale, come up, and turn to the left.
Put your bottom hand on a block, inside or outside your front foot.
Shorten your stance, and widen your feet for more balance.
Keep your top hand on your hip.
With lower back or sacrum pain, twist only a little and let your hips turn with you.
In pregnancy, skip closed twists. Take Triangle again instead.
Extended Side Angle
Utthita Pārśvakoṇāsana
Step your feet wide and turn your right toes out.
Bend your right knee until it’s directly over your ankle.
Place your right hand on the floor, outside your right foot.
Reach your left arm over your ear, one long line from your back heel to your fingertips.
Press your knee back into your arm, and open your chest.
Let your neck relax as you gaze up past your top hand.
Stay for five breaths. Breathe into the long side of your body.
Keep your front knee over your ankle. Don’t let it fall inward.
Inhale, come up, and turn to the left.
Rest your forearm on your thigh instead of your hand on the floor.
Put a block under your bottom hand.
Keep your top hand on your hip if your shoulder is tired.
With a knee injury, bend your front knee less and rest your forearm on your thigh.
With a neck injury, look down at the floor.
Revolved Side Angle
Parivṛtta Pārśvakoṇāsana
Turn to the right, turn your back foot in, and bend your front knee.
Exhale, twist and bring your left shoulder outside your right knee.
Place your left hand on the floor, outside your right foot.
Keep your back leg straight and press your back heel down.
Reach your right arm over your ear and turn your chest up.
Lengthen first, then let the twist grow from your belly.
Stay for five breaths. If your breath gets short, twist less.
Keep your front knee over your ankle as you twist.
Inhale, come up, and turn to the left.
Lower your back knee to the mat, and bring your hands together with your elbow outside your knee.
Put a block under your bottom hand, inside or outside your foot.
Lift your back heel if it won’t stay down.
With a lower back or sacrum problem, twist gently with your hands together at your chest.
With a knee injury, bend your front knee less.
In pregnancy, skip deep twists. Take Extended Side Angle again instead.
Wide-Legged Forward Fold
Prasārita Pādottānāsana
Step your feet wide apart, toes turned slightly in.
Exhale, place your hands on the floor between your feet, shoulder-width apart.
Inhale, look forward and lengthen your spine.
Exhale, bend your elbows straight back and lower the crown of your head toward the floor.
Draw your inner thighs back as you fold.
Let your neck soften and your head hang heavy.
Stay for five breaths, and let each exhale take you a little deeper.
Keep your weight in your feet, not on your head.
Inhale, look up. Exhale, hands to your waist. Inhale, come all the way up.
Rest your hands or forearms on blocks.
Bend your knees a little to ease the pull in the back of your legs.
In version C, hold a strap between your hands if they don’t meet behind you.

ujjayi
Breathe through your nose, with a soft ocean sound in your throat.
ashtanga
Yoga has eight limbs, and the poses are only one of them.
yama
The first limb is yama: how we treat others, on the mat and off it.
ahimsa

satya
Satya means being honest with yourself about how your body feels today.
asteya

brahmacharya
Brahmacharya on the mat: use the energy you need, and keep the rest.
aparigraha

niyama
The niyamas turn the practice inward, to how we treat ourselves.
saucha

santosha
Notice what already feels good in this pose. That is santosha.
tapas
Tapas is the heat of steady practice. Stay one more breath.
svadhyaya

ishvara pranidhana
Ishvara pranidhana: do your best, then let go of the result.
dhyana
Dhyana is meditation: attention that rests without effort.
samadhi
Samadhi is the last of the eight limbs. We don’t chase it; we prepare for it.
chakra
Bring your attention to the heart centre, the heart chakra.
mudra
Rest your hands in chin mudra, thumb and index finger touching.
mantra

om

shanti
Om, shanti, shanti, shanti. Peace, peace, peace.
sthira

sukha

prana
Feel the prana, the life energy, moving with each breath.
nadi
Alternate nostril breathing is nadi shodhana: clearing the channels.
anicca
Every sensation arises and passes away. Anicca.
dukkha
When we cling to what changes, dukkha follows.
anattā
This sensation is not me, not mine. It is just sensation.
sīla
Sila, kind and honest action, is the ground of meditation.
samādhi

paññā
Panna is not something we think. It is something we see for ourselves.
mettā
Let’s close with metta. May all beings be happy.
karuṇā
Meet your own pain with karuna, the way you would comfort a friend.
muditā

upekkhā

vedanā

saṅkhāra

saññā

viññāṇa

samatha

kamma

dhamma

jhāna

satipaṭṭhāna
